value.deck: GitHub now lets users turn off specific digital keys without shutting down entire applications or accounts.
shortVersion: When different software applications connect to each other, they use special digital keys to share access. If one key is lost or stolen, you need a quick way to turn it off. GitHub now lets people cancel just the specific type of key that was exposed.

Think of this like turning off a single lost keycard rather than changing every lock in your office building. This gives teams much finer control over their security. It protects accounts by limiting the damage if a single key gets compromised.
value.plainLanguage: GitHub updated its platform so people can cancel specific types of digital access keys without blocking everything else.

keyTerms.meaning: A piece of digital information, like a password or security key, used to prove who you are.
The act of officially canceling or turning off a digital access key so it can no longer be used.
A special digital pass that allows one computer program to talk to another securely.

value.whyItMatters: This change helps protect teams from major security headaches by making sure a single leaked key does not force you to shut down all your connected tools.
watchNext: Watch for more updates on how software platforms help teams manage their digital keys safely.
Look for new guidelines on how to handle security when connecting multiple apps together.
